mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in a month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in UNRATE above 7% predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor-market disengagement reduces consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations.
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE > 7% for ≥3 consecutive months, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in >70% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by more than 5% in the same month, it indicates strong demand pull, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption relative to production
failure_condition: Over a 2-year window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline of (GDPC1 - INDPRO > 5%) in 70% of such months (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least 3% in INDPRO over two months suggests weakening supply-side conditions, which precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates marginally higher valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls ≥3% in month t and again in month t+1
failure_condition: In >50% of such supply-side contraction episodes, the 20-day forward return is negative or flat.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL below 225 for three consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate cuts.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month deflationary window, the 5-day forward return is not statistically positive in >80% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly PAYEMS exceeds 140,000 by 10% from the prior month, it signals a surge in job creation that precedes a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 154,000 in a month (10% above previous month)
failure_condition: In >40% of such labor expansion episodes, the 20-day forward return is non-positive.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent monthly increases in HOUST (household spending) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their prior month's levels by at least 2% each are jointly predictive of a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to dual demand channels.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous_month and RSAFS > previous_month, each by ≥2% in the same month
failure_condition: In >75% of such dual-demand months, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a control group (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side loose policy (FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE < 5%) combined with a one-time 2% drop in INDPRO in the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates inventory build-up and weak demand.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND UNRATE < 5% AND INDPRO < previous_month in the same month
regime_hint: Supply-side loose policy regime with production contraction
failure_condition: In >50% of such episodes, the 20-day forward return is non-negative or the interaction terms fail to Granger-cause the forward return (p > 0.05).
